heroLede: I work in Security Operations at Checkout.com, investigating things that shouldn't have happened and building things to make sure they don't happen again. Well, ideally.
heroBody:
But that's just one worldline. In another, I'm usually taking things apart, building something new, or following a curiosity that turned into a six hour rabbit hole. Software, security, cloud, hardware. If it catches my interest, I'll probably experiment with it.

Sometimes it becomes a project. Sometimes a note in The Lab. Sometimes I just lose track of time.

Storm supervises. Occasionally.
roomHint: Poke around. Most things in here lead somewhere.
closingBody: Got a quest for me? Something you're building, something that broke in an interesting way, or just a question about something here? Write to me at
labIntro: Experiments, notes, investigations, and things I wanted to understand. Some are finished, some are still running, and a few are mostly lessons in what not to do.
workbenchIntro: Websites, tools and the occasional piece of hardware: things I've built, things I'm still building, and a few experiments that got slightly out of hand. Some were for other people; some were just to see whether I could.

aboutBody:
I'm Asad. I work in Security Operations at Checkout.com, where I spend a lot of time looking at what systems are doing and asking whether they should be.

I got here the long way round: software trainee, IT support, the service desk, then security. Each step taught me a bit more about how things fit together, and how many ways they can come apart.

Outside work I build things: small tools, scripts that automate the boring parts, the occasional bit of hardware. Most of it starts with *how does this actually work?* and ends somewhere I didn't plan.

The Lab is where I write those detours down. The name is a nod to *Steins;Gate*: a cramped lab, a few curious people, and experiments run mostly to see what happens.

And this is Storm, a fluffy tabby-and-white cat who has decided every warm spot near my desk is his. He's usually right.

If something here caught your eye, [say hello](mailto:contact@asad.atterkhan.com).
